sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报 DealBook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, days after being named Deputy Attorney General, Rod Rosenstein was so alarmed by what he was seeing inside the White House that he proposed a series of extreme measures.
sentences.zh: 今天，在被任命为副司法部长几天后，罗德·罗森斯坦对他在白宫内部所见的情况感到非常震惊，以至于他提出了一系列极端措施。

sentences.en: Will those proposals now cost him his job?
sentences.zh: 这些提议现在会让他丢掉工作吗？

sentences.en: And new allegations against Judge Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 还有针对布雷特·卡瓦诺法官的新指控。

sentences.en: Monday, September 24th.
sentences.zh: 9月24日，星期一。

sentences.en: Mike Schmidt, where did this most recent investigation start for you?
sentences.zh: 迈克·施密特，这次最新的调查是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: This has taken months to work on, if not even more than that.
sentences.zh: 这项工作花费了数月时间，甚至可能更久。

sentences.en: My colleague Adam Goleman and I set out to try and look at the period of time between when Jim Comey was fired in May of 2017
sentences.zh: 我和同事亚当·戈尔曼着手研究从2017年5月吉姆·科米被解雇

sentences.en: and when Bob Mueller was appointed as the special counsel.
sentences.zh: 到鲍勃·穆勒被任命为特别检察官之间的这段时间。

sentences.en: It's an eight-day period of time.
sentences.zh: 这是一段为期八天的时间。

sentences.en: What happened inside the Justice Department?
sentences.zh: 司法部内部发生了什么？

sentences.en: How did Rod Rosenstein, the Deputy Attorney General, who was overseeing the Russia investigation,
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦，那位负责监督俄罗斯调查的副司法部长，是如何

sentences.en: make the extraordinary and ultimately monumental decision to appoint Bob Mueller as a special counsel?
sentences.zh: 做出任命鲍勃·穆勒为特别检察官这一非同寻常且最终具有里程碑意义的决定的？

sentences.en: And, Mike, why did those eight days seem like an important period of time?
sentences.zh: 迈克，为什么这八天看起来是一个重要的时期？

sentences.en: In a sense, it was the time that time forgot.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是被时间遗忘的一段时间。

sentences.en: It was incredibly important how they came to that decision.
sentences.zh: 他们如何做出那个决定至关重要。

sentences.en: But it ends with Mueller being appointed, so it often got overlooked.
sentences.zh: 但它以穆勒被任命而告终，所以它经常被忽视。

sentences.en: And we never sort of turned around and looked back and said,
sentences.zh: 我们从来没有回过头来看一看并说，

sentences.en: OK, what happened after Comey was fired?
sentences.zh: 好吧，科米被解雇后发生了什么？

sentences.en: What did the FBI try and do?
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局试图做什么？

sentences.en: What was going through Rod Rosenstein's mind?
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦当时在想什么？

sentences.en: How did he come to appoint Mueller?
sentences.zh: 他是如何决定任命穆勒的？

sentences.en: And, Mike, why were you interested in Rod Rosenstein's role in all of this, in particular, during this eight-day period?
sentences.zh: 迈克，为什么你对罗德·罗森斯坦在这一切中的角色，特别是在这八天期间的角色感兴趣？

sentences.en: He was in this incredibly unique position because, as part of the Comey firing, he wrote a memo for the president that basically gave the rationale for it.
sentences.zh: 他处于一个极其独特的地位，因为作为科米被解雇事件的一部分，他为总统写了一份备忘录，基本上为解雇提供了理由。

sentences.en: America's brand-new Deputy Attorney General, Rod Rosenstein, provided the ammunition and the altitude for President Donald Trump to drop a political bombshell.
sentences.zh: 美国新任副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦，为唐纳德·特朗普总统投下一枚政治重磅炸弹提供了弹药和高度。

sentences.en: And his brand-new Deputy Attorney General, Rod Rosenstein, who has a bipartisan background, recommended to the president that the president fire James Comey as attorney general.
sentences.zh: 而他新任的副司法部长，具有两党背景的罗德·罗森斯坦，建议总统解雇司法部长詹姆斯·科米。

sentences.en: It appears to center around Comey's handling of the investigation into Hillary Clinton's emails, ironically enough.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，这似乎集中在科米处理希拉里·克林顿邮件调查的方式上。

sentences.en: It sharply criticized how Comey had handled the Clinton email investigation.
sentences.zh: 它严厉批评了科米处理克林顿邮件调查的方式。

sentences.en: The public lost trust in the FBI after Director Comey bungled the Hillary Clinton email case, he claiMs.
sentences.zh: 他声称，科米局长搞砸了希拉里·克林顿的邮件案后，公众对联邦调查局失去了信任。

sentences.en: I cannot defend the director's handling of the investigation, Rosenstein writes, and I do not understand his refusal to accept that he was mistaken.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦写道，我无法为局长处理调查的方式辩护，我也不理解他为何拒绝承认自己错了。

sentences.en: Then Comey gets fired and all of the criticism comes down on Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 然后科米被解雇了，所有的批评都落在了罗森斯坦身上。

sentences.en: The Democrats say, why is it that you helped the president come up with a sham reason to get rid of Comey?
sentences.zh: 民主党人说，你为什么帮助总统编造了一个除掉科米的虚假理由？

sentences.en: And how do we know that it's a sham reason, the justification in Rosenstein's letter?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道这是一个虚假理由，即罗森斯坦信中的辩解？

sentences.en: Well, it was never all that believable that the only reason that Trump fired Comey was because he was too mean to Hillary Clinton and had been too tough on her.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特朗普解雇科米的唯一原因是他对希拉里·克林顿太刻薄、对他太强硬，这从来都不太可信。

sentences.en: It was hard to believe that in the face or the backdrop of an investigation into ties between Donald Trump's campaign and Russia.
sentences.zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普竞选团队与俄罗斯之间存在联系的调查背景下，这很难让人相信。

sentences.en: And what happens in the days after Comey is fired is that Rosenstein is sharply criticized in the press for apparently creating this fake reason to fire Comey.
sentences.zh: 科米被解雇后的几天里，罗森斯坦因显然编造了这样一个解雇科米的虚假理由而在媒体上受到严厉批评。

sentences.en: Comey, the FBI begins pressuring Rosenstein behind the scenes to appoint a special counsel.
sentences.zh: 科米被解雇后，联邦调查局开始在幕后向罗森斯坦施压，要求任命一名特别检察官。

sentences.en: Rosenstein starts considering candidates.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦开始考虑人选。

sentences.en: And then on May 16th, we report that Comey had written a contemporaneous memo about an interaction he had with Trump.
sentences.zh: 然后在5月16日，我们报道说科米写了一份关于他与特朗普互动的同期备忘录。

sentences.en: A day after that story comes out, he appoints Mueller to be the special counsel.
sentences.zh: 在那篇报道出来一天后，他任命穆勒为特别检察官。

sentences.en: So at this point, a series of events, some of which Rosenstein has a little control over,
sentences.zh: 所以此时，一系列事件，其中一些罗森斯坦几乎无法控制，

sentences.en: like drafting a letter and others he doesn't, like the disclosure of the fact that the president asked Comey
sentences.zh: 比如起草一封信，而另一些他无法控制，比如总统要求科米

sentences.en: to end the investigation into Flynn, are all coming together and make Rosenstein feel like he has to appoint an independent investigator of this all.
sentences.zh: 结束对弗林的调查这一事实的披露，所有这些汇集在一起，让罗森斯坦觉得他必须任命一名独立的调查员来处理这一切。

sentences.en: Rosenstein apparently felt that there were too many questions about the independence of the investigation,
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦显然认为关于调查独立性的质疑太多了，

sentences.en: that he had to go to the next level to appoint a special counsel who has some protections from outside influence from the White House.
sentences.zh: 他必须更进一步，任命一名能够免受白宫外部影响的特别检察官。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's the backdrop for your latest reporting.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是你最新报道的背景。

sentences.en: What have you learned about this eight-day period?
sentences.zh: 关于这八天，你了解到了什么？

sentences.en: We've learned about the different measures that Rosenstein and others considered as they confronted the fallout from the Comey firing.
sentences.zh: 我们了解到罗森斯坦和其他人在面对科米被解雇后的后果时所考虑的不同措施。

sentences.en: They didn't completely understand the president's behavior.
sentences.zh: 他们并不完全理解总统的行为。

sentences.en: They weren't sure what he was up to.
sentences.zh: 他们不确定他在搞什么名堂。

sentences.en: They weren't sure that he may even be fit enough for the office.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不确定他是否适合担任这个职位。

sentences.en: And we have learned about some of those things they considered.
sentences.zh: 我们已经了解了他们考虑过的一些事情。

sentences.en: And what did they consider, particularly Rosenstein?
sentences.zh: 他们考虑了什么，特别是罗森斯坦？

sentences.en: Rosenstein raised the prospect of wearing a wire to record his conversations with the president.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦提出了佩戴窃听器来记录他与总统谈话的可能性。

sentences.en: And he spoke to FBI officials about the idea of trying to recruit others to invoke the 25th Amendment to oust the president from office.
sentences.zh: 他还与联邦调查局官员讨论了试图招募其他人援引第25修正案将总统赶下台的想法。

sentences.en: Mike, let's take these one at a time because they're pretty extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 迈克，我们一个一个来谈，因为这些建议非常惊人。

sentences.en: What was Rosenstein discussing with the president that he thought he needed a recording of?
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦在与总统讨论什么，以至于他认为需要录音？

sentences.en: Rosenstein thought that the president was not taking the process of picking a new FBI director as seriously as he should.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦认为总统没有像他应该做的那样认真对待挑选新联邦调查局局长的过程。

sentences.en: He thought that it was chaotic and emblematic of the larger dysfunction within the administration.
sentences.zh: 他认为这很混乱，是政府内部更大功能失调的象征。

sentences.en: And who did he make this suggestion in front of?
sentences.zh: 他在谁面前提出了这个建议？

sentences.en: Because it feels like the kind of thing you would say to very trusted people around you.
sentences.zh: 因为这听起来像是你会对身边非常信任的人说的话。

sentences.en: Rosenstein makes it in a meeting with senior federal law enforcement officials, officials at the top of the Justice Department and the FBI.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦是在与高级联邦执法官员、司法部和联邦调查局高层官员的会议上提出的。

sentences.en: So Rosenstein was thinking, I'll record these conversations with the president that alarm me,
sentences.zh: 所以罗森斯坦当时在想，我要记录下这些让我感到震惊的与总统的谈话，

sentences.en: that feel like they reflect some very problematic behaviors and instincts from this president in this moment.
sentences.zh: 这些谈话似乎反映了这位总统在这一时刻的一些非常令人不安的行为和本能。

sentences.en: And then I will do what exactly?
sentences.zh: 然后我到底要做什么？

sentences.en: It's not clear what he wanted to do with those recordings.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他想用这些录音做什么。

sentences.en: But what we do know Rosenstein was also talking about at the time was trying to recruit others to invoke the 25th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 但我们所知道的是，罗森斯坦当时也在谈论试图招募其他人来援引第25修正案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The second of his pretty extraordinary suggestions.
sentences.zh: 这是他那些非常惊人的建议中的第二个。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And to whom did Rosenstein make the suggestion of invoking the 25th Amendment?
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦向谁提出了援引第25修正案的建议？

sentences.en: It was made to Andrew McCabe, the acting FBI director at the time, who memorialized it in the contemporaneous memo he wrote.
sentences.zh: 这是向当时的代理联邦调查局局长安德鲁·麦凯布提出的，他在自己写的同期备忘录中记录了这一点。

sentences.en: And how would that have worked exactly, invoking the 25th Amendment?
sentences.zh: 那么援引第25修正案到底是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: To use it, you need for a portion of the cabinet and a portion of Congress to essentially declare that the president's unfit for office.
sentences.zh: 要使用它，你需要一部分内阁成员和一部分国会议员基本上宣布总统不适合担任公职。

sentences.en: And Rosenstein is saying that he believes he could recruit Attorney General Jeff Sessions and John Kelly,
sentences.zh: 而罗森斯坦说他相信他可以招募司法部长杰夫·塞申斯和约翰·凯利，

sentences.en: the secretary of the Department of Homeland Security at the time, who is now the White House chief of staff, to go along with this.
sentences.zh: 当时国土安全部部长，现在是白宫办公厅主任，来支持这一点。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: So he expressed some confidence that he believed he could bring those people along with him.
sentences.zh: 所以他表达了一些信心，相信他可以拉拢这些人加入他的行列。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: So how serious do you think that he was about this?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为他对此有多认真？

sentences.en: Is he kicking around an idea the way that the people do?
sentences.zh: 他是在像普通人那样随便说说吗？

sentences.en: Or is he actually proposing putting this into action?
sentences.zh: 还是他真的提议将此付诸行动？

sentences.en: Like, this is not an idea that Rosenstein was sort of batting around with his friends in a backyard barbecue.
sentences.zh: 这并不是罗森斯坦在后院烧烤时与朋友闲聊的那种想法。

sentences.en: It was something that he raised in a meeting with the top officials at the Justice Department and the FBI.
sentences.zh: 这是他在与司法部和联邦调查局高层官员的会议上提出的事情。

sentences.en: Which in and of itself conveys a certain level of seriousness.
sentences.zh: 这本身就传达了一种严肃的程度。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: Comey has just been fired.
sentences.zh: 科米刚刚被解雇。

sentences.en: They're trying to figure out what to do.
sentences.zh: 他们正在试图弄清楚该做什么。

sentences.en: And he really struggled in the moment.
sentences.zh: 他在那一刻确实很挣扎。

sentences.en: He was seen as unnerved.
sentences.zh: 他看起来很不安。

sentences.en: He got emotional.
sentences.zh: 他情绪激动。

sentences.en: And he was under enormous amount of pressure.
sentences.zh: 他承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: He was being criticized in the press at a level that he had never seen of himself before.
sentences.zh: 他在媒体上受到了前所未有的批评。

sentences.en: And he was essentially the top law enforcement official because the attorney general had been recused from the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 而且他基本上是最高执法官员，因为司法部长已经回避了俄罗斯调查。

sentences.en: So it's all resting on his shoulders.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都压在他的肩上。

sentences.en: And Rosenstein here is making a decision of whether to escalate the Russia investigation to a level that he knows will completely alter the trajectory of Donald Trump's presidency.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦在这里做出了一个决定，是否要将俄罗斯调查升级到一个他知道会彻底改变唐纳德·特朗普总统任期轨迹的水平。

sentences.en: And what's our understanding of why all this talk never seems to have gone anywhere and turned into action?
sentences.zh: 我们对为什么所有这些谈话似乎都没有进展并付诸行动有什么了解？

sentences.en: I think that some folks thought that these ideas were pretty off the wall and went too far.
sentences.zh: 我认为有些人认为这些想法相当疯狂，走得太远了。

sentences.en: And ultimately Rosenstein makes an extraordinary decision and that's to appoint Mueller.
sentences.zh: 最终罗森斯坦做出了一个非同寻常的决定，那就是任命穆勒。

sentences.en: And that is the way the questions around Trump's firing of Comey are dealt with.
sentences.zh: 这就是处理围绕特朗普解雇科米的问题的方式。

sentences.en: So after proposing these two pretty extreme proposals, he ends up during this eight-day period settling on a more conventional route,
sentences.zh: 所以在提出这两个相当极端的建议后，他在那八天期间最终决定采取一条更常规的路线，

sentences.en: which is appointing a special counsel who will investigate everything that's been happening and not require these more exotic solutions.
sentences.zh: 那就是任命一名特别检察官，他将调查正在发生的一切，而不需要这些更奇特的解决方案。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: But we also don't know what else Rosenstein may have done.
sentences.zh: 但我们也确实不知道罗森斯坦还可能做了什么。

sentences.en: All we're talking about here are two ideas that were raised and ultimately, as far as we know, not followed through on.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里谈论的只是两个被提出来，据我们所知最终没有付诸实施的想法。

sentences.en: What we do know is that he ends up appointing Mueller as the special counsel.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，他最终任命穆勒为特别检察官。

sentences.en: And by doing that, sort of having a prosecutor who has some protections from the political whims of the president and the White House,
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，拥有了一位能够免受总统和白宫政治意愿影响的检察官，

sentences.en: that this will be an investigation conducted free of politics.
sentences.zh: 这将是一项不受政治影响的调查。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜总会用黑胶唱片打碟的时代，每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个，就像，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼表出品的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 一个月的时间让你越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能得到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Tonight there are so many questions.
sentences.zh: 今晚有太多的问题。

sentences.en: How was this said?
sentences.zh: 这些话是怎么说的？

sentences.en: How serious were these suggestions?
sentences.zh: 这些建议有多认真？

sentences.en: And tonight, Rosenstein himself now responding.
sentences.zh: 今晚，罗森斯坦本人现在做出了回应。

sentences.en: Rosenstein vehemently denying the claims, saying in a statement,
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦强烈否认这些指控，并在声明中表示，

sentences.en: The New York Times story is inaccurate and factually incorrect.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的报道是不准确的，事实也是错误的。

sentences.en: I will not further comment on a story based on anonymous sources who are obviously biased against the department and are advancing their own personal agenda.
sentences.zh: 我不会再对一篇基于匿名来源的报道发表评论，这些来源显然对司法部有偏见，并正在推进他们自己的个人议程。

sentences.en: I don't know where the standard is at The New York Times, but when it's just anonymous all the time and they're just willing to run with it, it seems outrageous.
sentences.zh: 我不知道《纽约时报》的标准在哪里，但当它总是匿名，而且他们只是愿意随波逐流时，这看起来太离谱了。

sentences.en: Who do you think might have been motivated to leak this information to The New York Times?
sentences.zh: 你认为谁可能有动机向《纽约时报》泄露这些信息？

sentences.en: That's sort of the nuts of what are being speculated about right now.
sentences.zh: 这正是目前人们猜测的核心所在。

sentences.en: I wonder if it's coming from someone who wants Rosenstein fired because it obviously doesn't make him look very good.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否来自一个想要罗森斯坦被解雇的人，因为这显然让他看起来不太好。

sentences.en: The Times says their sources are people who were briefed on the fact that Rod Rosenstein had said that to other officials and sources who were briefed on a memo.
sentences.zh: 《时报》称他们的消息来源是那些被告知罗德·罗森斯坦曾对其他官员说过这些话的人，以及那些被告知备忘录内容的消息来源。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the response to this reporting in the past few days, because there has been a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们谈谈过去几天对这篇报道的反应，因为反应非常多。

sentences.en: What has been the response from Rosenstein himself?
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦本人的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Rosenstein contested the story and said it was not accurate.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦对这篇报道提出了异议，并表示它不准确。

sentences.en: The Justice Department provided us with a anonymous official who was in the room at the time of the meeting who said that Rosenstein had raised the idea of wearing a wire to record conversations with the president,
sentences.zh: 司法部向我们提供了一位当时在会议室里的匿名官员，他说罗森斯坦确实提出了佩戴窃听器来记录与总统谈话的想法，

sentences.en: but that he had done so sarcastically.
sentences.zh: 但他这样做是讽刺性的。

sentences.en: That did not add up with the totality of our other reporting, which was that Rosenstein was serious when he said it.
sentences.zh: 这与我们其他报道的全部内容不符，我们的报道称罗森斯坦在说那番话时是认真的。

sentences.en: He had been asked in the meeting whether he was joking.
sentences.zh: 他在会上被问到是否在开玩笑。

sentences.en: He said that he was not and then raised the prospect of wiring up FBI officials who were going in themselves to meet with Trump about being the next director.
sentences.zh: 他说他没有开玩笑，随后提出了给那些即将去见特朗普、商谈接任局长职位的联邦调查局官员身上安装窃听器的想法。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The government putting forward an additional source in response to reporting does not seem like a conventional tactic.
sentences.zh: 政府为了回应报道而额外推出一个消息源，这看起来并不像是一种常规策略。

sentences.en: I can't think of many times I've heard of that happening before.
sentences.zh: 我想不出以前有什么时候听说过这种情况。

sentences.en: The Justice Department and the White House went to great lengths to try and undermine this story.
sentences.zh: 司法部和白宫曾竭尽全力试图破坏这篇报道。

sentences.en: Rosenstein sees himself as a protector of Mueller.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦将自己视为穆勒的保护者。

sentences.en: And there is a fear that if anything happens to Rosenstein, the president could more easily make a move against Mueller,
sentences.zh: 人们担心，如果罗森斯坦出了什么事，总统就能更容易地对穆勒采取行动，

sentences.en: restrain Mueller or get rid of Mueller and the investigation.
sentences.zh: 限制穆勒，或者除掉穆勒和他的调查。

sentences.en: So the Justice Department tried to undermine the story to try and prevent this notion from taking hold.
sentences.zh: 所以司法部试图破坏这篇报道，以防止这种想法扎根。

sentences.en: And the White House tried to undermine the idea that the 25th Amendment was discussed because that is something the president is incredibly sensitive to.
sentences.zh: 而白宫试图否定讨论过《第25修正案》的说法，因为总统对这一点极其敏感。

sentences.en: So the response is not actually what you might expect.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种反应其实并不出人意料。

sentences.en: It's not just the White House trying to deny this story to save face.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是白宫为了挽回面子而试图否认这篇报道。

sentences.en: It's also the Justice Department trying to downplay it to protect the special counsel, Robert Mueller, and his ability to do this investigation.
sentences.zh: 这也是司法部为了保护特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒及其进行这项调查的能力，而试图淡化此事。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're trying to protect Rosenstein as much as possible to create doubt about the story so the president doesn't turn around and get rid of Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 他们正竭尽全力保护罗森斯坦，试图让人们对报道产生怀疑，这样总统就不会转过头来除掉罗森斯坦。

sentences.en: And getting rid of Rosenstein could theoretically mean eventually getting rid of Mueller.
sentences.zh: 而除掉罗森斯坦，理论上就意味着最终除掉穆勒。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the fear that if you got rid of Rosenstein, who has gone to great lengths to protect Mueller,
sentences.zh: 这就是人们的担忧：如果你除掉了竭尽全力保护穆勒的罗森斯坦，

sentences.en: Trump would try and get a political ally in there who would do what Trump wants, which is end the investigation.
sentences.zh: 特朗普就会试图安插一个政治盟友进去，做特朗普想做的事，也就是结束调查。

sentences.en: And, Mike, what do you say to what this additional source that the Department of Justice is putting forward is claiming?
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，对于司法部推出的这位额外消息源的说法，你怎么看？

sentences.en: What's your response to that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有何回应？

sentences.en: On this, we sort of ended up with two buckets of reporting.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我们最终得到了两类报道。

sentences.en: In one of them was the anonymous official the Justice Department gave us who said that they were in the meeting and that Rosenstein had been sarcastic.
sentences.zh: 其中一类是司法部提供给我们的匿名官员，他说他当时在会上，罗森斯坦是在讽刺。

sentences.en: In suggesting the wearing of the wire.
sentences.zh: 在建议安装窃听器这件事上。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the other bucket was a wide range of reporting that involved speaking to many different people who my colleague Adam Goldman and I thought had more credibility and more detail about what occurred and provided us with evidence that Rosenstein had indeed been asked whether it was a joke and had dismissed it.
sentences.zh: 另一类是广泛的报道，涉及与许多不同的人交谈，我和我的同事亚当·戈德曼认为这些人更可信，对发生的事情了解得更详细，并向我们提供了证据，证明罗森斯坦确实被问到这是否是个玩笑，并且他予以了否认。

sentences.en: When you say evidence, what kind of evidence can anyone ever provide about a meeting that was many, many months ago?
sentences.zh: 当你提到证据时，对于一个发生在许多许多个月前的会议，任何人能提供什么样的证据呢？

sentences.en: These meetings were memorialized in FBI memos at the time that documented conversations that Andrew McCabe, the acting FBI director, had with Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 这些会议在当时被记录在联邦调查局的备忘录中，记录了代理局长安德鲁·麦凯布与罗森斯坦的谈话。

sentences.en: So, Mike, as a reporter, you're weighing two things at this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克，作为一名记者，你此刻正在权衡两件事。

sentences.en: The single source put forward by the Department of Justice who claims that this suggestion was sarcastic and interviews and documents,
sentences.zh: 司法部推出的单一消息源声称该建议是讽刺性的，以及采访和文件，

sentences.en: including McCabe's memorialized notes from these meetings, suggesting that they were quite serious.
sentences.zh: 包括麦凯布对这些会议的记录，都表明他们是非常认真的。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you as a reporter decide that there is more weight to the collective reporting of these sources and these mellows.
sentences.zh: 听起来作为记者，你认为这些消息源和备忘录的集体报道更有分量。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: With unnamed source reporting, where we are relying on people to speak under the condition of anonymity to us,
sentences.zh: 在匿名消息源的报道中，我们依赖人们在匿名条件下与我们交谈，

sentences.en: we are forced to weigh a wide range of different things when we come to the determination about how to use that information.
sentences.zh: 当我们决定如何使用这些信息时，我们被迫权衡各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: How specific was the information?
sentences.zh: 这些信息有多具体？

sentences.en: What was the person's motivation?
sentences.zh: 这个人的动机是什么？

sentences.en: How reliable have they been in the past?
sentences.zh: 他们过去表现得有多可靠？

sentences.en: And how much does it fit into the larger narrative of other things that we understand were going on at the time?
sentences.zh: 它在多大程度上符合我们所了解的当时发生的其他事情的宏观叙事？

sentences.en: Does this sort of fit into other stories or other reporting that we have?
sentences.zh: 这是否符合我们掌握的其他故事或报道？

sentences.en: Does this help fill out the picture in a way that sort of makes sense?
sentences.zh: 这是否有助于以一种合理的方式拼凑出全貌？

sentences.en: And what about the 25th Amendment suggestion?
sentences.zh: 那么关于《第25修正案》的建议呢？

sentences.en: Has Rosenstein or anyone at the Department of Justice at all suggested that that was done in a sarcastic manner?
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦或司法部的任何人是否暗示过那是开玩笑的？

sentences.en: The Justice Department has put no one forward to say that the discussions about the 25th Amendment were done in jeSt.
sentences.zh: 司法部没有推出任何人来说关于《第25修正案》的讨论是开玩笑的。

sentences.en: Rosenstein did put out a second statement in which he said he had never advocated for removing the president.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦确实发表了第二份声明，称他从未主张罢免总统。

sentences.en: Well, that wording seems very intriguing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种措辞听起来非常耐人寻味。

sentences.en: He said he had never advocated using the 25th Amendment, but he's not saying that he didn't propose it.
sentences.zh: 他说他从未主张使用《第25修正案》，但他并没有说他没有提议过。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'll let Rosenstein speak for himself on that.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我让罗森斯坦自己说吧。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So I also want to talk about the public response to this reporting because it's been really intense on both sides.
sentences.zh: 我还想谈谈公众对这篇报道的反应，因为双方的反应都非常强烈。

sentences.en: On the one hand, people on the left would be very uncomfortable with that happening because of what that might mean for the future of the Mueller investigation,
sentences.zh: 一方面，左派人士会因为这件事而感到非常不安，因为这可能意味着穆勒调查的未来将受到影响，

sentences.en: as we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的那样。

sentences.en: On the other hand, people on the right would be uncomfortable because if Trump fires Rosenstein, it could potentially add to possible evidence of obstruction of justice,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，右派人士会感到不安，因为如果特朗普解雇罗森斯坦，这可能会增加妨碍司法的潜在证据，

sentences.en: which began with the firing of Comey.
sentences.zh: 而妨碍司法始于解雇科米。

sentences.en: So a lot of people seem to not like this reporting.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人似乎不喜欢这篇报道。

sentences.en: Yeah, I understand that as we follow the different threads of the Trump story, every piece of reporting is not going to be accepted with open arMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，我理解，当我们追踪特朗普故事的不同线索时，并非每一篇报道都会受到热烈欢迎。

sentences.en: And that's certainly the case here.
sentences.zh: 这种情况确实如此。

sentences.en: But that's not really our job.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是我们的工作。

sentences.en: Our job is to dive in to what happened and come to a place where we feel confident about the facts that we have.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作是深入挖掘发生了什么，并得出一个我们对所掌握的事实感到自信的结论。

sentences.en: Finally, Mike, let's talk about the likelihood that Trump actually does fire Rosenstein, which is what both sides of this fear.
sentences.zh: 最后，迈克，我们来谈谈特朗普真的解雇罗森斯坦的可能性，这是双方都担心的。

sentences.en: What do you expect is going to happen here?
sentences.zh: 你预计这里会发生什么？

sentences.en: Is Rosenstein now a marked man?
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦现在是一个被盯上的人吗？

sentences.en: Many people believe that.
sentences.zh: 很多人都这么认为。

sentences.en: I got a call on Friday night from someone fairly close to the president who said, why is it that the president hasn't done anything against Rosenstein?
sentences.zh: 周五晚上我接到一个与总统关系相当密切的人的电话，他说，为什么总统没有对罗森斯坦采取任何行动？

sentences.en: We don't understand this.
sentences.zh: 我们不明白这一点。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I said, well, you know the president a lot better than I do and you have a lot more access to him than we do.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你比我更了解总统，而且你接触他的机会比我们多得多。

sentences.en: So what do you think?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Well, we just don't understand what's going on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们只是不明白发生了什么。

sentences.en: We thought that he would get very angry and try and do something.
sentences.zh: 我们以为他会非常生气并试图做点什么。

sentences.en: Our colleague Maggie Haberman has done reporting that shows that the president has been sort of even tempered about this.
sentences.zh: 我们的同事玛吉·哈伯曼的报道显示，总统对此一直保持着相对冷静的态度。

sentences.en: And why do we think that would be?
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, the president has wanted to get rid of Rosenstein and Sessions for over a year now since when Mueller was appointed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，自穆勒被任命以来，总统已经有一年多想除掉罗森斯坦和塞申斯了。

sentences.en: What we do know is that even before the story, he was planning to get rid of them after the midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，甚至在这篇报道之前，他就计划在期中选举后除掉他们。

sentences.en: That happens at the beginning of November.
sentences.zh: 那是在11月初。

sentences.en: We're almost there.
sentences.zh: 快到了。

sentences.en: And the president probably figures if I've waited this long, I might as well continue to wait a little bit longer.
sentences.zh: 总统可能觉得既然我已经等了这么久，不妨再多等一会儿。

sentences.en: So he may essentially be biding his time.
sentences.zh: 所以他可能本质上是在等待时机。

sentences.en: It looks like it, at least for now.
sentences.zh: 看起来是这样，至少目前如此。

sentences.en: You know, as we're talking about all this,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们谈论这一切时，

sentences.en: I can't help thinking of the op-ed that the Times ran about two weeks ago written by a senior administration official who also recounted a discussion of taking pretty extreme measures to oust the president,
sentences.zh: 我不禁想起了《泰晤士报》大约两周前刊登的一篇专栏文章，作者是一位政府高级官员，他也讲述了关于采取极端措施罢免总统的讨论，

sentences.en: including invoking the 25th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 包括援引《第25修正案》。

sentences.en: And neither of us know who wrote that op-ed.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都不知道是谁写了那篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: But if we believe that there is some kind of a Trump resistance from within the administration, given what you've now reported,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们相信政府内部存在某种特朗普抵抗力量，鉴于你现在的报道，

sentences.en: is it fair to say that the deputy attorney general of the United States, Rod Rosenstein, is a part of that?
sentences.zh: 可以说美国副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦是其中的一部分吗？

sentences.en: I don't know whether he's a part of that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他是否是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: But what we do know is that in May of 2017, less than four months after Donald Trump took office, his senior officials were already talking about the 25th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 但我们所知道的是，在2017年5月，即唐纳德·特朗普上任不到四个月后，他的高级官员们就已经在讨论《第25修正案》了。

sentences.en: We're already talking about whether or not they should try to end his presidency.
sentences.zh: 已经在讨论是否应该试图结束他的总统任期。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Michael, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: On Sunday, after nearly a week of tense negotiations,
sentences.zh: 周日，经过近一周的紧张谈判，

sentences.en: Christine Blasey Ford agreed to testify before the Senate Judiciary Committee about her allegations against Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀·布莱西·福特同意在参议院司法委员会前就她对最高法院提名人布雷特·卡瓦诺的指控作证。

sentences.en: Dr. Blasey had originally asked for the FBI to investigate her claim that Kavanaugh sexually assaulted her in high school before she would agree to testify,
sentences.zh: 布莱西博士最初要求联邦调查局调查她关于卡瓦诺在高中时性侵她的指控，然后才同意作证，

sentences.en: but has since backed down from that demand.
sentences.zh: 但后来放弃了这一要求。

sentences.en: Several details surrounding the public hearing, now scheduled for Thursday, remain unresolved, including whether senators or their staff will question Dr. Blasey.
sentences.zh: 围绕定于周四举行的公开听证会的几个细节仍未解决，包括参议员还是他们的工作人员将质询布莱西博士。

sentences.en: But in a statement, her lawyer said that those issues, quote, will not impede the hearing taking place.
sentences.zh: 但在声明中，她的律师表示，这些问题“不会阻碍听证会的进行”。

sentences.en: Do you have an open mind on this?
sentences.zh: 你对此持开放态度吗？

sentences.en: And is there anything that Dr. Ford could say that would persuade you to vote against Kavanaugh's nomination?
sentences.zh: 福特博士说的话有没有可能说服你投票反对卡瓦诺的提名？

sentences.en: Honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说。

sentences.en: On Sunday, a Republican member of the Judiciary Committee, Senator Lindsey Graham, said he did not expect Dr. Blasey's testimony to change his support for Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 周日，司法委员会的一名共和党成员、参议员林赛·格雷厄姆表示，他不认为布莱西博士的证词会改变他对卡瓦诺的支持。

sentences.en: I'm just being honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我只是实话实说。

sentences.en: Unless there's something more, no, I'm not going to ruin Judge Kavanaugh's life over this.
sentences.zh: 除非有更多证据，否则不，我不会因为这件事毁了卡瓦诺法官的一生。

sentences.en: But she should come forward.
sentences.zh: 但她应该站出来。

sentences.en: She should have her say.
sentences.zh: 她应该有发言权。

sentences.en: She will be respectfully treated.
sentences.zh: 她会受到尊重的对待。

sentences.en: A few hours later, The New Yorker reported that Senate Democrats are investigating a new claim of sexual misconduct against Kavanaugh from his time as an undergraduate at Yale.
sentences.zh: 几个小时后，《纽约客》报道称，参议院民主党人正在调查卡瓦诺在耶鲁大学本科期间的一项新的性不端指控。

sentences.en: Deborah Ramirez told the magazine that during a drunken party, Kavanaugh thrust his penis into her face as she pushed him away.
sentences.zh: 黛博拉·拉米雷斯告诉该杂志，在一次醉酒派对上，卡瓦诺把他的生殖器塞到她脸上，她把他推开了。

sentences.en: In response, the ranking Democrat on the Judiciary Committee, Dianne Feinstein,
sentences.zh: 作为回应，司法委员会的民主党领袖黛安·范斯坦，

sentences.en: called for postponing Thursday's hearing with Dr. Blasey and asked that the FBI investigate the latest allegations.
sentences.zh: 呼吁推迟周四与布莱西博士的听证会，并要求联邦调查局调查最新的指控。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。
